clue.text: Imposing condition which covers irregular use (quarterly)

indicators.note: covers means the word for condition is wrapped round the other pieces like a lid

parts.note: a condition or situation is a state

indicators.note: irregular means the letters of use are not in their usual order and must be rearranged

parts.note: qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for quarterly

explanation.surface: A forbidding rule that governs occasional use, reviewed every quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges USE to UES; with QU (quarterly) that goes inside STATE, which 'covers' them. 'Imposing' looks like a verb for the condition, but it is the adjective defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tall, dignified and statue-like in bearing is impressive, commanding in appearance.

clue.text: Broken piece is difficult to put together

parts.note: S is a common abbreviation for is
something difficult is hard

explanation.surface: A broken fragment proves hard to fit back together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment of broken pottery or glass is called by this name.

clue.text: make reparation

annotationWithheld.why: The clue is held only as 'make reparation' (9): that defines ATONE, a verb, not the noun ATONEMENT, so the start of the clue and its wordplay are missing and no scan or search gives the rest.

clue.text: Totally flexible arrangement suggested by general visiting disreputable bar

parts.note: universal means general, applying to all
a joint is slang for a seedy bar or club

explanation.surface: A relaxed set-up dreamt up by an army general dropping into a dodgy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like the army officer but is the adjective meaning all-embracing; 'visiting' just links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This mechanical coupling lets a shaft transmit drive while bending in any direction, so it is flexible every way.

clue.text: Faddish diets, or meta drug?

indicators.note: faddish suggests fickle and changeable, so the letters of the words that follow are shuffled

explanation.surface: Are faddy diets, or some trendy pill, the answer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faddish' rearranges DIETS OR. The printed 'meta' appears to be an OCR misreading of the original wording and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic compounds of this class are taken medicinally or abused by athletes, so it is a kind of medicine or substance.

clue.text: Develops new sheep-station in America?

indicators.note: in means the new sheep enclosure is set inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America
a fold is a pen where sheep are kept

explanation.surface: A fresh sheep ranch is being developed somewhere in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheep-station' suggests an Australian ranch, but it is just a pen; 'in America' puts N + FOLD inside US.
explanation.definitionFit: A story or situation that develops gradually reveals itself, opening out as a flower does.

clue.text: Big blow for Ullswater? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only a part of the lake's name is used, a run of its inner letters

explanation.surface: A huge gust whips across the Lake District's Ullswater, though not the whole lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Ullswater is a lake in England's Lake District; the run is inside its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy slap or hit, such as one aimed at a fly, is a smack of this kind.

clue.text: Arab engaged in climbing tree becomes fatigued

indicators.note: engaged in means the Arab abbreviation is held inside the reversed tree
climbing in a down clue means the tree's name reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the yew is an evergreen tree
Ar. is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: An Arab clambering up a tree is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns YEW to WEY in this down entry, and 'engaged in' puts AR inside it; 'becomes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tired and drained of energy is the same as feeling exhausted.

clue.text: Toy boy initially putting on female undergarment to attract attention

parts.note: a teddy is a one-piece woman's undergarment

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of boy is used

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A toyboy pulls on lingerie to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy boy' reads as a young lover, but 'Toy' is the definition and 'boy initially' gives B, placed under TEDDY in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plush, stuffed animal is a children's plaything.

clue.text: The way people go on!

parts.note: reads as an exasperated remark about how folk behave, but literally describes a route walkers travel along

explanation.definitionFit: A right of way open to all walkers is a route for pedestrians.

clue.text: Irresponsible action with drug, a poison

indicators.note: irresponsible means behaving wildly, so the letters of action are thrown into disorder

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Reckless behaviour with drugs leads to poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irresponsible' rearranges ACTION to ACONIT, then E (ecstasy) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood or wolfsbane, a plant with a toxic root, is this toxin's source.

clue.text: Scarf, superior French article found in car

indicators.note: found in means the superior and French pieces sit inside the car maker's name

parts.note: a Ford is a make of car
U means upper class or superior
la is the French for the feminine 'the'

explanation.surface: A posh French scarf turns up inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'superior' is the British upper-class label (U and non-U).
explanation.definitionFit: A light silk or silk-cotton fabric, or a neckerchief made of it, carries this name.

clue.text: Taxi driver

parts.note: reads as a cabbie, but means the fuel that powers a cab's engine

explanation.definitionFit: Heavy fuel for compression-ignition engines is what most cabs run on.

clue.text: Bay possibly blocked by front and rear of lorry

definitions.text: Bay possibly blocked by front and rear of lorry

indicators.note: blocked by means the rearranged bay is shut in between the letters taken from lorry
front and rear means the first and last letters of lorry
possibly means the letters of bay may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A roadside bay is obstructed by a parked lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BAY to AYB, which goes between L and Y, the first and last letters of 'lorry'. The whole clue also defines it: a lorry parks in this roadside bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pull-in where vehicles can stop off the carriageway is a stopping bay of this sort.

clue.text: Drive, for instance, is leading to grounds

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in addresses
eg stands for exempli gratia, for instance
S is a common abbreviation for is

explanation.surface: A driveway, say, leads to a property's grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' suggests estate land, but means coffee grounds or sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment left at the bottom of a cup or bottle is residue of this kind.

clue.text: Cleaner takes endless relaxation having put in a bit of work

indicators.note: having put in means the unit of work is inserted into the shortened relaxation word
endless means the final letter of the relaxation word is dropped

parts.note: detente is a relaxation of tension between states
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A cleaner, after doing a little work, takes a never-ending rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts DETENTE to DETENT, and 'having put in' places ERG inside it; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing powder or liquid soap is a cleansing agent.

clue.text: Profane deed oddly associated with secondary class

indicators.note: oddly means take the first and third letters of deed

parts.note: sec. is an abbreviation for secondary
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A blasphemous act linked to a second-rate group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profane' could be an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to violate something sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a holy place or object with violent disrespect is to violate its sanctity.

clue.text: Smooth, white table as ordered for interior of antechamber

indicators.note: for interior of means the rearranged letters replace everything inside the outer letters of antechamber

parts.note: the first and last letters of antechamber are A and R, the shell left once its interior goes

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of table as are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A smooth white table is ordered for the inside of an entrance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges TABLE AS to LABASTE, which becomes the inside of 'antechamber', leaving its first and last letters A and R round it.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine-grained translucent stone, a form of gypsum, is proverbially pale and smooth, as in skin described that way.

clue.text: I work in gallery to provide some stimulation

indicators.note: in means the I and the work word are placed inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A gallery employee promises a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the famous London art gallery; 'work' means cultivate land, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite someone pleasurably, often in a teasing way, is to arouse them.

clue.text: One of the possible starters, in dark green

explanation.surface: A choice of first course, served in deep green.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear-shaped fruit is a common first course, and its skin's colour names a dull deep green shade.

clue.text: Mid-table fixture?

parts.note: reads as a league match between middling teams, but means an ornament fixed in the centre of a dining table

explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental centrepiece with branching dishes for fruit stands at the middle of a dinner table.

clue.text: Old Norse song showing

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for Norse
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: An ancient Norse ballad is being performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' means being broadcast at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme being broadcast now is being transmitted live.

clue.text: Set commercial in exotic resort

indicators.note: in means the advert goes inside the resort's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a glamorous holiday destination
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: An advert is filmed in a far-off holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is the noun: a receiver, as in a wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless receiver is an apparatus for hearing broadcasts.

clue.text: Man cleared from charges goes out

indicators.note: cleared from means the word man is removed from the longer word

parts.note: mandates are charges or commissions given to someone
taken literally as the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone acquitted of the charges leaves the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man cleared from charges' reads as an acquittal, but MAN is taken out of MANDATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sees a partner romantically is courting them.

clue.text: Do too much swimming practice, maybe, in open water?

definitions.text: Do too much swimming practice, maybe

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Is training at the open-water swimming spot overdoing it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in open water' suggests a lake swim, but splits into OVERT + RAIN, with 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise an athlete beyond what helps is to push training too far.

clue.text: Tender runs off end of line

indicators.note: off means the letters of runs are disordered, gone off course
end of means the last letter of line

explanation.surface: A rail tender running off at the end of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges RUNS to NURS, and 'end of line' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend means to care for the sick, as a carer on a ward does.

clue.text: Established on island a nation-state

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation is founded on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: This Baltic republic is a sovereign country.

clue.text: Greek with the name of being a corrupt type

parts.note: named after means bearing the name of

explanation.surface: A Greek reputed to be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who profits dishonestly from public office is a swindler; in British use the word also means a hard worker.

clue.text: Throw at the wicket

parts.note: reads as a fielder's shy at the stumps, but means the coin spin captains make on the pitch before a cricket match

explanation.definitionFit: A coin flipped before play decides which side bats first.

clue.text: On which we hang things to dry?

definitions.text: On which we hang things to dry?

parts.words: On which we hang things to dry?
parts.note: reads as a washing line, but describes a frame that stands in a bathroom for hanging cloths

explanation.definitionFit: A freestanding rail or frame holds bath linen while it airs.
